editorial.headline: Glassware Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23121 covers household glassware, display pieces, and glass or crystal containers, with foreign ownership open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23121 is the industrial home for making glass objects that sit close to daily life: cups, drinking glasses, plates, bowls, teapots, jars, ashtrays, and baby milk bottles. Its scope also reaches beyond utility into display and decorative glass, including glass statues or figures, vases, crystal lamps, pressure-lamp chimneys, and wall-lamp chimneys. The same activity group includes the making of glass and crystal containers or packaging, such as bottles and jars, including hollow glass. In practical terms, this is not retailing glassware or merely trading finished stock; it is the manufacturing activity behind household, decorative, and container glass products.

The scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification can serve anything from a small workshop producing household glass items to a larger industrial operation making containers or display pieces. That breadth matters because the same KBLI title carries both everyday domestic objects and more formal glass or crystal packaging. A founder using this code should read it through the manufacturing acts named in the scope: making the items, shaping the output category, and staying within household glassware, decorative glass objects, and glass or crystal containers.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, so the national reading is not a partial opening. For a foreign-owned setup, the central point is that KBLI 23121 is recorded as open to PMA at up to full foreign ownership. Nothing in the record adds a minimum capital figure, operating threshold, special deadline, or separate licence condition, so none should be assumed from the classification alone.

Bali does not change that outcome into a closure. The province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record marks KBLI 23121 as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says its OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the honest national-versus-Bali picture: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic. The classification still needs to be kept close to the activity itself: manufacturing household glassware, decorative glass pieces, and glass or crystal containers, not a broader glass business by implication.
